what: On first load, a background-colored cover over the screen holds for .3s, then lifts over .6s sine.out. A gradient cover tinted pale indigo only at the top is pushed down .3s later over .7s, so its tinted edge exits upward. On a same-site link click, after .5s the gradient comes down over .4s to tint the top, and the background cover fills in .2s later over .7s before navigating — a calm, whitening handoff

options.hold: Seconds from opening until it clears, default .3 — set 0 for screens opened often, like an app
options.slide: Gradient fade-out (sec), default .7 · lag is its delay, default .3
options.wait: Time from link click to start of cover (sec), default .5 — 0 for app
options.on: If manual, the side using the initial reveal handles it (when only covering via el.fxCover(href))
options.nav: When off, links are not intercepted (whoever uses a transition like barba calls el.fxCover())
options.[data-fx-part=veil]·[data-fx-part=sweep]: Background color layer · gradient layer (two children, nothing is applied if absent)
options.fx:done: Event the element fires once fully cleared (bubbles up to the document)

from.where: shared.js .nm-loader (original #js-pageloader — 300ms after load, .js-pageloader__all alpha 0 over .6s sine.out · __gradient background-position 100% 100% over .7s sine.out delayed .3s / on barba leave: after .5s (+.6 if the menu is open) the gradient goes 100% 100% → 100% 0% over .4s, and __all autoAlpha 0 → 1 over .7s, another .2s later)

note: In the original the curtain (z 99) sits below the header menu (z 999), so the fixed left menu stays visible throughout the transition — the user sets it with z-index (default 9000)
